issues.body:
In all six routers the selected-destination row injects an argument-ignoring probe:

    chk("route: private repo + token wins",
        _alert_route("p/r", "tok", "reg/reg", lambda r, t: True) == ("p/r", "tok"))

The same shape appears in dispatch-stall-alert.py, groom-mint-alert.py, metrics-alert.py, park-stock-alert.py (`#1775: a positively verified private destination is selected`) and triage-stock-alert.py.

Only the negative direction is pinned: the same-repo row asserts `calls == []`. Nothing asserts the probe is invoked with the ALERT repo under the ALERT token. So `check(registry_repo, alert_token)`, `check(alert_repo, None)`, or an argument transposition all survive every new assertion while the live deployment verifies the visibility of the WRONG repository — which then silently never selects the private destination at all.

`_private_probe_rows` does not cover this: it pins the argv of `_repo_confirmed_private` itself, given a repo/token it supplies directly. The binding from `_alert_route`'s parameters into `check(...)` is the untested seam.

The merged reference implementation of this exact router already kills this mutant — scripts/groom-alert.py:211-212 asserts `vis_calls == [("org/private", "tok")]` beside its positive row. This PR is one row below its own precedent, in six files.
issues.fix_hint:
In each of the six modules, capture the probe arguments on the positive row instead of discarding them, mirroring groom-alert.py:206-212:

    vis_calls = []
    chk("route: private repo + token wins",
        _alert_route("p/r", "tok", "reg/reg",
                     lambda r, t: vis_calls.append((r, t)) or True) == ("p/r", "tok"))
    chk("route: the visibility check runs against the ALERT repo under the ALERT token",
        vis_calls == [("p/r", "tok")])

Use each file's existing `chk` signature (2-arg boolean in ci-latency-alert.py, 3-arg got/want elsewhere).
issues.title: The positive route rows never pin WHICH (repo, token) the visibility probe is called with

issues.body:
The diff teaches three live-path harnesses to answer the probe, always with `private: true`:

- park-stock-alert.py `_test_route_wiring.fake_run`: `if cmd[1:3] == ["api", f"repos/{PRIVATE}"]: return _Result(0, json.dumps({"private": True}))`
- metrics-alert.py `_test_gh_flows.run_main`: `responses[("api", "repos/org/private")] = _Result(0, json.dumps({"private": True}))`
- groom-mint-alert.py `_test_gh_flows.fake_run`: the same branch

No assertion consumes any of them. Every wiring row is membership-based (`find(...)`, `sub in subs()`), so:

1. There is NO run in which the probe answers `private: false` and the row asserts the alert still lands, on the REGISTRY, and never under ALERT_TOKEN. That is the entire behaviour this PR adds, and it is unreachable from main() in all six scripts.
2. Replacing `_alert_route`'s default with a constant-true — the precise regression back to presence-only routing — keeps every self-test in all six files green.

Again the merged precedent already does this: scripts/groom-alert.py:354-372 runs main() with `alert_repo="org/public", visibility='{"private": false}'` and asserts `("org/registry", False, ("api", "repos/org/public") in subs())`, then asserts a same-repo ALERT_REPO spends NO probe end-to-end (`[s for s in subs() if s[0] == "api"] == []`).

An injected stub that no row reads is a conditionally-inert fixture — the shape this repo's own harnesses call out (`an instrument that cannot fire has said nothing`).
issues.fix_hint:
Parameterise the probe answer in each of the three harnesses and add the two missing rows, per groom-alert.py:354-372.

park-stock-alert.py `_test_route_wiring`: add `visibility` to `state`, return it from the `repos/{PRIVATE}` branch, then:

    run_once(PRIVATE, ALERT_TOK, visibility='{"private": false}')
    chk("#1775 wiring: an UNVERIFIED destination -> registry fallback, alert still lands, "
        "never under ALERT_TOKEN, and the probe WAS spent",
        (routed("issue", "create") == (REGISTRY, ambient()),
         routed("issue", "create")[1] == ALERT_TOK,
         any(c[1:3] == ["api", f"repos/{PRIVATE}"] for c, _e in calls)),
        (True, False, True))
    run_once(REGISTRY.upper(), ALERT_TOK)
    chk("#1775 wiring: same-repo ALERT_REPO -> registry, and NO probe is spent",
        (routed("issue", "create")[0], [c for c, _e in calls if c[1] == "api"
                                        and "/pulls?" not in c[2]]),
        (REGISTRY, []))

Do the equivalent in metrics-alert.py `_test_gh_flows` (add a `visibility` kwarg to `run_main`, assert on `find(("api", "repos/org/public"))` and `subs()`) and groom-mint-alert.py `_test_gh_flows`. ci-latency-alert.py, dispatch-stall-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py have no main()-level route harness; for those the fix in the first issue is the minimum.
issues.title: Probe stubs were added to three main() harnesses but nothing asserts them — the fail-closed path is never exercised end-to-end

issues.body:
The four rewritten docstrings (dispatch-stall-alert.py, ci-latency-alert.py, groom-mint-alert.py, metrics-alert.py) assert they are `identical semantics and signature to the other alert routers`. After this diff two routers still implement presence-only selection:

- scripts/ratelimit-alert.py:363 — `def _alert_route(alert_repo, alert_token, registry_repo)` with `if alert_repo and alert_token: return alert_repo, alert_token`
- scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py:245 — the same

So the blanket claim is inaccurate as written. It also cuts the other way: ratelimit-alert.py:364 documents itself as `identical semantics to groom-alert/ci-latency-alert/park-stock-alert`, and this diff makes all three of those named siblings behave differently from it. Neither is caught by CI — ratelimit-alert.py and ledger-identity-watch.py pin only their own docstrings, so this is stale prose rather than a red test, but it is prose the park/triage EQUALITY guards exist specifically to keep honest.

This is a scope observation, not a demand to convert all thirteen routers in one PR.
issues.fix_hint: Either name the verified set explicitly (e.g. `identical semantics and signature to the verified routers in groom-alert.py / usage-alert.py / worker-pr.py`) rather than `the other alert routers`, or extend the migration to scripts/ratelimit-alert.py and scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py in this PR. If the latter is deferred, correcting ratelimit-alert.py:364's now-false cross-reference is a one-line follow-up worth filing.
issues.title: "identical semantics and signature to the other alert routers" is now false for two siblings the PR leaves behind

issues.body:
`_private_probe_rows` rebinds the module-global `_gh` and is named without a `_test_` prefix, so `_test_authority_ceiling` (groom-mint-alert.py:1540-1542) and the equivalent `_test_no_hold_labels` in dispatch-stall-alert.py:1145-1147 and metrics-alert.py scan it as production code.

It is benign today — I checked: its literals (`'{"private": true}'`, `"org/private"`, `"route-token"`, `"Result"`) match neither the `needs:|status:|role:|review:|priority:|area:` deny-list nor `{merge, pr, --auto, --admin, --squash}`, and its only list literals are empty, so `argv_heads` is unchanged. But a helper whose whole job is to swap out the module's single gh entry point does not belong in the half those guards are asserting about, and it is dead weight in the shipped script.

The same applies in ci-latency-alert.py, metrics-alert.py, park-stock-alert.py, triage-stock-alert.py and dispatch-stall-alert.py.
issues.fix_hint: Rename to `_test_private_probe_rows` (or move the body inline into each `_self_test`) so the existing `node.name.startswith("_test_")` exclusion covers it. Calling it from `_self_test` is unchanged; it takes no `chk`, so it does not need to join the `_test_*(chk)` dispatch table.
issues.title: `_private_probe_rows` is a test-only global monkeypatcher that ships in the LIVE half of the module

issues.body:
The new structural row pins `api_shapes == [(2, True, "repos/", False)]`. The fourth element, `any(word in {"-X", "--method", "-f", "--input"} for word in words)`, is computed over `words` — the Constant elements of the argv list. Because the first element of the same tuple pins `len(argv.elts) == 2`, any call carrying a flag already reds on the length. So the flag clause is always `False` and can never independently catch anything.

It is also incomplete on its own terms: `-F`, `--field` and `--raw-field` are gh's other mutation-bearing flags and are absent from the set.

The guard as a whole is sound — the length pin plus the `"repos/"` JoinedStr prefix genuinely constrains the widened `api` vocabulary to a single two-argument GET — so this is a dead sub-assertion, not a hole.
issues.fix_hint: Either drop the fourth tuple element as redundant, or make it load-bearing by relaxing the length pin to `len(argv.elts) >= 2` and completing the flag set with `-F`, `--field`, `--raw-field`. Do not do both.
issues.title: The mutation-flag element of the `api_shapes` pin cannot fire

issues.body:
The copy in ci-latency-alert.py is written out normally with a docstring; the copies in triage-stock-alert.py, dispatch-stall-alert.py, groom-mint-alert.py, metrics-alert.py and park-stock-alert.py compress statements onto shared lines (`_gh = response(rc, body); values.append(...)`, `finally: _gh = original`) and drop the docstring.

There is no flake8/ruff config or lint job in .github/workflows, so nothing goes red — this is purely a readability inconsistency in six copies of what is meant to be one identical helper.
issues.fix_hint: Expand the five compressed copies to match ci-latency-alert.py's formatting, including its `"""Exercise every fail-closed result of this module's live repository probe."""` docstring, so the six copies stay diffable against each other.
issues.title: `_private_probe_rows` is semicolon-compressed in five of six copies

verdict.summary:
The change is directionally right and mostly well built: it propagates the already-merged #432/#436 positively-verified-private-route pattern (ALERT_TOKEN present AND case-insensitively distinct from the registry AND a live GET /repos/{ALERT_REPO} confirming a literal private:true) from groom-alert.py/usage-alert.py/worker-pr.py into six more alert routers. I verified: `json` and a compatible `_gh(args, capture, token)` exist in all six modules; `_repo_confirmed_private` fails closed on rc!=0, empty/unparseable body, and every non-`True` `private` value (`"true"`, `1`, `[]`, `"yes"`); `same_repo` handles `registry_repo=None`; each module has exactly ONE production call site passing no `confirmed_private`; the `_private_probe_rows` rows are genuinely non-vacuous (five distinct outcomes plus the exact argv/kwargs of the gh call). The structural guards still hold: metrics-alert's `nouns/verbs` widening to `api` is compensated by a real `api_shapes` pin (exactly one 2-arg `repos/` JoinedStr read), dispatch-stall's and groom-mint's `argv_heads` already contained `api`, and the park/triage docstring EQUALITY pins were updated on both sides with a live anchor. park-stock-alert's `ambient()`/census fix correctly disambiguates the new probe call from the `/pulls?` read.

What blocks approval is test non-vacuity measured against this repo's own bar, not against an invented one. groom-alert.py — the merged reference implementation of exactly this router — kills two mutants that none of the six copies here kill: (1) it pins that the visibility check is invoked with (ALERT_REPO, ALERT_TOKEN), and (2) it drives an UNVERIFIABLE destination end-to-end through main() and asserts the alert lands on the registry, not under ALERT_TOKEN, with the probe demonstrably issued.
